docRequirement: claude-directory.md:304 binds custom COMMAND files (the `commands/` folder card, `fix-issue.md` example) to the same argument substitution as skills: "`$ARGUMENTS` substitutes whatever you typed after the command name. For positional access, use `$0` `$1` and so on." The same page states it for skills at :222. `slash-commands.md` is byte-identical to `skills.md` (verified 2026-08-03, same md5), whose note at :16 makes the binding explicit — "Custom commands have been merged into skills. A file at `.claude/commands/deploy.md` and a skill at `.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` both create `/deploy` and work the same way" — so the substitution table applies to command bodies too: `$ARGUMENTS[N]` 0-based (:301), `$N` as its shorthand where `$0` is the FIRST argument (:302), shell-style quoting of the tail (:327), an indexed placeholder with no argument "stays in the content unchanged" (:329), and a single backslash escaping the token (:331).
current: Skills comply; commands do not, and the two halves are separate implementations. SKILLS: `matchArgumentPlaceholder` + `expandSkillArguments` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/runtime-skill-content.ts:497-600) resolve `$ARGUMENTS[N]` (:507-515), `$ARGUMENTS` (:517-520), declared `$name` (:527-538) and bare `$N` (:539-548, `values[Number(...)]`, undefined left literal) in one left-to-right pass with backslash escaping (:577-585); the quote-aware tail split is `splitSkillArguments` (:455-478); the `ARGUMENTS: <value>` append fallback is at :692-698. COMMANDS: the single expansion chokepoint is `packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:334` — `modelMessage = command.body.replace(/\$ARGUMENTS|\{\{args\}\}/g, () => args)` — one regex over two tokens, with the comment at :329-332 stating that only those two are substituted. Every non-MCP command source funnels through it: native `.nessy-agent/commands` and `.agents/commands` (packages/shared/src/slash-commands/custom-commands.ts:59-62 `COMMAND_DIRS`, body returned unmodified by `parseCustomCommand` at :148-170), plugin prompt-commands (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:16165 `materializer.readText(...).trim()`), workflow commands (`workflowSlashCommandBody`, custom-commands.ts:272) and skill commands (`skillSlashCommandBody`, custom-commands.ts:302). `modelMessage` is handed to `sessionManager.sendMessage` as the 10th positional argument (sessions.ts:373) and is what the model actually receives (SessionManager.ts:15120-15121), so nothing downstream re-expands it. The fork positively knows commands lack this: `DYNAMIC_SUBSTITUTION_PATTERNS` (packages/shared/src/plugins/format-adapters/claude.ts:653-657) carries `{ pattern: /\$[1-9]\b/, kind: 'positional-argument' }` and pushes `plugin.deferred.claude_command_dynamic_substitution` at :741-749 with the comment "Never evaluate shell/file expressions — only detect and defer them". Native command frontmatter is a flat `Record<string, string>` (custom-commands.ts:104-131) and only `description`/`model` are read (:157-158), so the `arguments` frontmatter (`$name`) is not parsed either. MCP prompt commands are correctly exempt — `mapMcpPromptArguments` (custom-commands.ts:375-385, via `parseQuotedArgs` :359) maps the quote-aware tail onto declared parameters at resolution time (SessionManager.ts:16100) and the rendered body carries no tokens.
divergence: Not a wrong key name and not a missing value: the positional family is simply not implemented on the command path. `$ARGUMENTS` and the legacy Nessy `{{args}}` expand correctly; `$0`, `$1`, `$ARGUMENTS[N]` and `\$1` escaping do not, so those placeholders reach the model as literal text. The correct 0-based, quote-aware, single-pass implementation the page describes already exists 200 lines away in `runtime-skill-content.ts` but is module-private and reachable only from the skill materializer. Second-order: the plugin importer's detector for the same construct is `/\$[1-9]\b/`, which misses `$0` (the FIRST argument per skills.md:302) and `$ARGUMENTS[N]` entirely, and native plus workflow commands get no deferral notice at all.

change.what: Add `export` (or export a thin alias `expandArgumentPlaceholders`) so the command path reuses this exact matcher instead of growing a second one. Nothing else in the file changes: `splitSkillArguments` (:455) and `matchArgumentPlaceholder` (:497) stay private behind it, and the skills-only `ARGUMENTS: <value>` append at :692-698 stays where it is — the returned `sawArgumentsToken` flag lets the command path ignore it. No export-map edit needed: `./capabilities/runtime-skill-content` is already in packages/shared/package.json exports and server-core already imports the module at SessionManager.ts:277.

Replace the single regex with two statements: normalize the legacy token in the AUTHORED body first — `const body = command.body.replace(/\{\{args\}\}/g, () => '$ARGUMENTS')` — then `modelMessage = expandSkillArguments(body, args, []).text`. Order matters: normalizing the body (never the arguments) keeps the one-pass guarantee the comment at :329-332 promises, because the expander writes substituted text to the output and never re-scans it, so an argument containing `$0` or `{{args}}` stays inert. Third argument is `[]` — no declared names on the command path (see notes). Rewrite the :329-332 comment to name the family actually supported ($ARGUMENTS, $ARGUMENTS[N], $N, backslash escape, legacy {{args}}) and keep the "no shell, no env/file interpolation" sentence.

Delete the `{ pattern: /\$[1-9]\b/, kind: 'positional-argument' }` row once the sessions.ts change lands — otherwise every imported Claude command using `$1` keeps emitting `plugin.deferred.claude_command_dynamic_substitution` for a capability we now support, which is a false compatibility warning. The `bash-execution` and `file-reference` rows are unrelated and stay. One-line deletion plus its comment.

The adapter edit changes only the CONTENT of a plugin compatibility report's `deferred` array, read by `blockedInstallMessage` (apps/electron/src/renderer/pages/PluginsPage.tsx:1850-1858) and format-adapters.test.ts:2207. userImpact: A custom command that uses positional placeholders silently loses every argument. Concrete: `.nessy-agent/commands/migrate.md` containing `Migrate the $0 component from $1 to $2.`, invoked as `/migrate SearchBar React Vue` — the composer shows `/migrate SearchBar React Vue`, but the model-facing turn body is the unchanged sentence with literal `$0 $1 $2` (modelMessage replaces the visible message for the model, SessionManager.ts:15120-15121), so the model is asked to migrate a component named `$0` and never sees SearchBar/React/Vue at all. Same for an imported Claude plugin command written against `$1` (a common shape in the official catalogues): it installs with no visible warning — the `plugin.deferred.claude_command_dynamic_substitution` entry surfaces only inside the blocked-install toast (PluginsPage.tsx:1856), and a successful install never shows it — then behaves as if the user typed no arguments. `\$1.00` in prose also arrives with the backslash still attached. The same placeholders in a `/skill-name` invocation work correctly, which makes the failure look arbitrary to the user.
